audits.title: National audit of the blood transfusion process in the UK.
audits.standard: Standard procedures for administration of blood and national transfusion guidelines
audits.setting: National audit: 50 UK hospitals in first audit, 23 of the same hospitals in second (National Blood Service with Royal Colleges and Societies)

cycle1.result: Over 20% of hospitals had no Hospital Transfusion Committee; only one-third trained doctors in blood sampling; considerable variation in performance of standard procedures for administration of blood.

cycle2.result: Little change in practice between the two audits.

audits.other_findings: Audit tools were developed and published and fed into national guidelines on administration of blood; sample sizes are numbers of hospitals.
audits.citation: Murphy MF, Wilkinson J, Lowe D, Pearson M. National audit of the blood transfusion process in the UK. Transfus Med. 2001;11(5):363-370. doi:10.1046/j.1365-3148.2001.00330.x. PMID: 11696229.

audits.title: Audit of transfusion procedures in 660 hospitals. A College of American Pathologists Q-Probes study of patient identification and vital sign monitoring frequencies in 16494 transfusions.
audits.standard: Laboratory and blood bank accreditation requirements for patient identification (4 components) and vital sign monitoring (3 intervals)
audits.setting: 660 institutions in the College of American Pathologists Q-Probes programme, mainly United States

cycle1.result: First study: all identification components performed in 62.3% and all vital sign monitoring in 81.6% of transfusions (institution medians 69.0% and 90.2%).

cycle2.result: Second study: all identification performed in 25.4% and all monitoring in 88.3% (institution medians 10.0% and 95.0%).

audits.other_findings: Better compliance was linked to bedside transport of units, wristbands, reading identification aloud, written checklists, staff instruction and routine auditing. The two studies were separate, not before-and-after.
audits.citation: Novis DA, Miller KA, Howanitz PJ, Renner SW, Walsh MK, College of American Pathologists. Audit of transfusion procedures in 660 hospitals. A College of American Pathologists Q-Probes study of patient identification and vital sign monitoring frequencies in 16494 transfusions. Arch Pathol Lab Med. 2003;127(5):541-548. doi:10.5858/2003-127-0541-aotpih. PMID: 12708895.

audits.title: One year clinical audit of the use of blood and blood components at a tertiary hospital in Nigeria.
audits.standard: Appropriateness judged by a haematologist against clinical state and transfusion needs

cycle1.result: 29% of transfusions for moderate anaemia and 36% of FFP transfusions unnecessary; 81% of platelet transfusions inappropriate.

audits.other_findings: Severe anaemia was the commonest indication (38%); local guidelines recommended.
audits.citation: Arewa OP. One year clinical audit of the use of blood and blood components at a tertiary hospital in Nigeria. Niger J Clin Pract. 2009;12(4):429-433. PMID: 20329686.

audits.title: National audit of bedside transfusion practice.
audits.standard: Best practice for patient identification and monitoring during transfusion
audits.setting: National audit (Better Blood Transfusion, National Services Scotland)

cycle1.result: Most patients received safe transfusion with adequate identity checks and monitoring, but some lacked an identity wristband or monitoring (no figures given in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Continued improving trend compared with previous audits.
audits.citation: Cottrell S, Davidson V. National audit of bedside transfusion practice. Nurs Stand. 2013;27(43):41-48. doi:10.7748/ns2013.06.27.43.41.e7067. PMID: 23987720.

audits.title: Audit of pediatric transfusion practices in a tertiary care hospital.
audits.standard: British Committee for Standards in Haematology and American Association of Blood Banks guidelines
audits.setting: Department of Pathology and Blood Bank, Lady Hardinge Medical College, tertiary care hospital, New Delhi

cycle1.result: Appropriate use of blood components 59.65% (2,145 units in 1,819 episodes); whole blood most appropriately transfused (82.9%).

audits.other_findings: Red cells appropriately used in anaemias (73.14%) but inappropriately in surgery (53.6%); regular re-audit recommended.
audits.citation: Bahadur S, Sethi N, Pahuja S, Pathak C, Jain M. Audit of pediatric transfusion practices in a tertiary care hospital. Indian J Pediatr. 2015;82(4):333-339. doi:10.1007/s12098-014-1370-2. PMID: 24794324.

audits.title: Transfusion audit of blood products using the World Health Organization Basic Information Sheet in Qazvin, Islamic Republic of Iran.
audits.standard: Local and national transfusion guidelines; WHO Basic Information Sheet

cycle1.result: Adequate documentation in 62.6% of transfusion episodes (range 41%-73%); inappropriate requests: red cells and whole blood 15.7%, platelets 40.8%, FFP 34.1%.

audits.title: An Audit on Overnight Transfusion Practice in A Teaching Hospital in Malaysia.
audits.standard: Transfusion completion within 4 hours; overnight transfusion only for clinical need
audits.setting: Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia Medical Centre, Kuala Lumpur; teaching hospital

cycle1.result: 216 (16.8%) were overnight transfusions; indication acute 82.9%, less acute 13.9%, none 3.2%; average delay 5 h 40 min from crossmatch to start.

audits.other_findings: Poor patient monitoring during overnight transfusion and breaches of the 4-hour infusion rule.
audits.citation: Tang YL, Yousuf R, Wan Nawawi WM, Rahman IL, Zainal Abidin J, Rechard Nathan VR, et al.. An Audit on Overnight Transfusion Practice in A Teaching Hospital in Malaysia. Malays J Pathol. 2019;41(2):161-167. PMID: 31427551.

audits.title: Audit of pre-transfusion testing practices in hospital blood banks across Tanzania: A national survey.

cycle1.result: ABO/Rh typing and cross-matching available in all (100%); antibody screening in 13/31 (42.0%); tile method for ABO typing in 2/31 (6.5%); critical reagents available in 21/31 (67.7%); blood warming SOPs in 9 (29.0%) and FFP thawing SOPs in 14 (45.2%).

audits.other_findings: All facilities had SOPs for basic tests; phased recommendations were made.
audits.citation: Mwashiuya OF, Lyimo MA, Mogela DJ, Bhombo AJ, Mwimo JL, Shewiyo EJ, et al.. Audit of pre-transfusion testing practices in hospital blood banks across Tanzania: A national survey. Afr J Lab Med. 2026;15(1):2986. doi:10.4102/ajlm.v15i1.2986. PMID: 41647931.

audits.title: Quality assurance of clinical transfusion practice by implementation of the privilege of blood prescription and computerized prospective audit of blood requests.
audits.standard: Hospital guidelines for the proper use of blood
audits.setting: Large multispecialty hospital, IRCCS Ospedale Maggiore, Milan

cycle1.result: Perioperative patients given both red cells and plasma: 47.6% (320/672). Inappropriate plasma requests for elective general surgery 39% at programme onset.

audits.intervention: Non-urgent blood prescription restricted to a limited group of trained physicians, plus computerised prospective audit of all blood requests against guidelines.

cycle2.result: Red cells plus plasma: 37.8% (244/646), difference -9.8% (95% CI -4.5% to -15.1%), P<0.005. Inappropriate plasma requests fell to 14% in last trimester. 7884 requests audited: 96.8% red cell and 98.1% platelet requests appropriate.

audits.other_findings: About 27% of plasma requests did not comply, mainly for lack of evidence of coagulopathy.
audits.citation: Marconi M, Almini D, Pizzi MN, Riccardi D, Bergamaschi W, Giovanetti AM, et al.. Quality assurance of clinical transfusion practice by implementation of the privilege of blood prescription and computerized prospective audit of blood requests. Transfus Med. 1996;6(1):11-19. doi:10.1046/j.1365-3148.1996.d01-48.x. PMID: 8696443.
